title: An early H-alpha fit gives an uncertain 4.5 percent later error gain for GJ 3323 extraction differences
abstract: We test whether a stable linear activity response predicts a known difference between two GJ 3323 velocity extractions. A H-alpha slope fitted to 55 early HARPS exposures reduces weighted squared error by 4.55 percent in 66 later exposures. Time-bin resampling of both seasons gives ranges of -35.99 to 13.24 percent for 10-day bins and -23.55 to 10.33 percent for 30-day bins. Line width, wavelength dependence and joint fits also give ranges that include zero. The test does not establish a stable linear activity cause. It does not exclude changing activity, calibration effects or planets. The reductions share spectra, and no new independent observations are added. Code, aggregate results, exact source hashes, a figure and separate-data retrieval steps are included. The external database is excluded.

display.caption: Early activity slopes tested in the later season. Dots give point gains. Lines give time-bin resampling ranges. All ranges include zero.
